fullPassage: Everyone loves getting something for free, and these days it is easier than ever to receive a variety of free items. Companies give away free food, free T-shirts, even free cell phones. This might not seem like a smart thing for businesses to do, but it’s actually a well-planned strategy based on something called “freeconomics.” One basic practice of freeconomics is letting people try something once in order to make them become regular customers. For example, if you are given a free coffee at a café one morning, you might come back day after day to buy the same drink. This is the same reason a company might send you a small container of shampoo in the mail—they hope you will buy a full bottle the next time you go shopping. Another strategy of freeconomics is to give consumers something for free, knowing they will then need to purchase something to accompany it. A phone company, for example, may give you a free cell phone, but you then need to pay for an annual plan. The concept of freeconomics has been around for a while, but the Internet has made it more popular than ever. Because the cost of running an online business is so low, websites are constantly offering free benefits in the hope of attracting more visitors. Although some people will simply take advantage of the free offerings, the business may be able to convince them to upgrade to more attractive paid services. This is known as the “freemium” strategy, a combination of the words “free” and “premium.” Some experts believe freeconomics will eventually change the way business takes place. Already, any company with a superior product can benefit by giving potential consumers a free taste. And online, there are plenty of businesses, such as YouTube and Google, that don’t need to sell anything to consumers at all. They simply attract millions of people to their websites with free services, and then they make their profits from charging other companies to advertise on their site. These businesses make money, and we get to enjoy something for free.

questions.passage: Everyone loves getting something for free, and these days it is easier than ever to receive a variety of free items. Companies give away free food, free T-shirts, even free cell phones. This might not seem like a smart thing for businesses to do, but it’s actually a well-planned strategy based on something called “freeconomics.” One basic practice of freeconomics is letting people try something once in order to make them become regular customers. For example, if you are given a free coffee at a café one morning, you might come back day after day to buy the same drink. This is the same reason a company might send you a small container of shampoo in the mail—they hope you will buy a full bottle the next time you go shopping. Another strategy of freeconomics is to give consumers something for free, knowing they will then need to purchase something to accompany it. A phone company, for example, may give you a free cell phone, but you then need to pay for an annual plan. The concept of freeconomics has been around for a while, but the Internet has made it more popular than ever. Because the cost of running an online business is so low, websites are constantly offering free benefits in the hope of attracting more visitors. Although some people will simply take advantage of the free offerings, the business may be able to convince them to upgrade to more attractive paid services. This is known as the “freemium” strategy, a combination of the words “free” and “premium.” Some experts believe freeconomics will eventually change the way business takes place. Already, any company with a superior product can benefit by giving potential consumers a free taste. And online, there are plenty of businesses, such as YouTube and Google, that don’t need to sell anything to consumers at all. They simply attract millions of people to their websites with free services, and then they make their profits from charging other companies to advertise on their site. These businesses make money, and we get to enjoy something for free.

questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오. (영어로)

[ and / businesses / enjoy / for / free / get / make / money / something / to / we / These ] (12단어)

det.korean: '이런 사업체들은 돈을 벌고, 우리는 공짜로 무언가를 즐긴다'를 두 절의 병렬(and)로 배열해요.
det.analysis:
첫 절의 주어는 These businesses(이런 사업체들), 동사구는 make money(돈을 번다)예요.

→ and로 두 번째 절 we get to enjoy something for free(우리는 공짜로 무언가를 즐긴다)를 이어요.

→ 완성: These businesses make money and we get to enjoy something for free
det.tip: 절A and 절B = 병렬 (make money ~ and we get to enjoy ~).

questions.wa: These businesses make money and we get to enjoy something for free
accept: These businesses make money and we get to enjoy something for free

questions.passage: Everyone loves getting something for free, and these days it is easier than ever to receive a variety of free items. Companies give away free food, free T-shirts, even free cell phones. This might not seem like a smart thing for businesses to do, but it’s actually a well-planned strategy based on something called “freeconomics.” __________ in order to make them become regular customers. For example, if you are given a free coffee at a café one morning, you might come back day after day to buy the same drink. This is the same reason a company might send you a small container of shampoo in the mail—they hope you will buy a full bottle the next time you go shopping. Another strategy of freeconomics is to give consumers something for free, knowing they will then need to purchase something to accompany it. A phone company, for example, may give you a free cell phone, but you then need to pay for an annual plan. The concept of freeconomics has been around for a while, but the Internet has made it more popular than ever. Because the cost of running an online business is so low, websites are constantly offering free benefits in the hope of attracting more visitors. Although some people will simply take advantage of the free offerings, the business may be able to convince them to upgrade to more attractive paid services. This is known as the “freemium” strategy, a combination of the words “free” and “premium.” Some experts believe freeconomics will eventually change the way business takes place. Already, any company with a superior product can benefit by giving potential consumers a free taste. And online, there are plenty of businesses, such as YouTube and Google, that don’t need to sell anything to consumers at all. They simply attract millions of people to their websites with free services, and then they make their profits from charging other companies to advertise on their site. These businesses make money, and we get to enjoy something for free.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]의 단어를 모두 사용하여 (영어로) 쓰시오.

프리코노믹스의 한 가지 기본 관행은 사람들이 무언가를 한 번 시도해 보게 하는 것이다.
[조건] (1) basic, freeconomics, is, letting, of, once, One, people, practice, something, try 를 모두 사용 (2) 11단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: '~하게 하는 것이다'를 be동사 + 동명사(letting)로 영작해요.
det.analysis:
주어는 One basic practice of freeconomics(프리코노믹스의 한 기본 관행)예요.

→ 동사는 is, 보어로 동명사 letting을 써서 '~하게 하는 것'을 나타내요.

→ 'let + 목적어 + 동사원형' 구조로 letting people try something once로 마무리해요.

→ 완성: One basic practice of freeconomics is letting people try something once
det.tip: is letting + 목적어 + 동사원형 = ~하게 하는 것이다.

questions.wa: One basic practice of freeconomics is letting people try something once
accept: One basic practice of freeconomics is letting people try something once
